## 債市主線

美國職缺與工廠訂單優於預期，扭轉油價下跌帶動的早盤漲勢，也打斷債市近期的回升。10年期美債殖利率上升4.96個基點至4.9621%，主要由實質殖利率推動。半導體股反彈，也使當天市場不再那麼偏向防禦，但投資人對支應人工智慧投資熱潮的融資，仍要求相當高的報酬補償。

Meta完成當天美國唯一一筆投資級債券發行，募得$150億，訂單最高達$580億。其10年期債券殖利率為6.55%，比同為AA評級的債券高近1個百分點。這筆交易同時呈現需求強勁與融資昂貴兩個面向：投資人願意提供資金，但融資條件反映出他們對產業支出需求日益升高的疑慮。

相較於單靠股市反彈，經濟數據為利率上行提供了更扎實的依據。9月職缺超過市場預期，8月數字也獲上修；工廠訂單同樣優於預期，而且強勢不只來自飛機。這兩項數據都未顯示各類雇主或產業全面加速，但其細項使市場更難直接假設美國需求即將惡化。另一方面，澳洲意見分歧的升息決定，以及歐洲官員最新談話，顯示央行仍在持續通膨與愈來愈明顯的經濟活動制約之間權衡。

## 勞動需求扭轉美債漲勢

油價原先為公債買盤再添一項理由。WTI一度跌破每桶$94，創三週低點，10年期美債殖利率也曾下降約2個基點。但9月職缺與勞動力流動調查（JOLTS）公布後，走勢隨即逆轉。依Bloomberg盤中報導，數據出爐數分鐘內，10年期殖利率便觸及當天高點4.97%，日內升幅超過5個基點。ING的Padhraic Garvey認為數據強勁，殖利率上升是合理反應。

收盤時各期限殖利率普遍上升，以中期券升幅最明顯。5年期上升5.32個基點至4.7623%，2年期上升3.72個基點至4.6309%，30年期上升4.08個基點至5.3265%。2年與10年期利差擴大1.24個基點至33.12個基點，屬於債券下跌過程中的溫和曲線陡峭化，而非最短天期附息券出現格外劇烈的重新定價。

10年期抗通膨債券（TIPS）實質殖利率上升4.47個基點至2.6542%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則僅上升0.49個基點至2.3079%。名目殖利率升幅多數來自實質殖利率，顯示當天市場更關注需求韌性的證據，而非長期通膨補償再度急升。布蘭特原油收跌0.33%，報$104.42；WTI則回升至$96.76，收漲0.31%。

儘管當天反轉，美債此前的回升仍保留了大半。10年期殖利率較一週前低3.46個基點，較一個月前低31.09個基點。2年期殖利率一週下降10.6個基點，30年期卻上升1.62個基點。長端在這波週線漲勢中表現相對落後，使曲線同時對經濟展望及政府舉債的期限配置保持敏感。

JOLTS數值明顯優於預期，但官方對整體勞動市場的評估較為保守。9月職缺達752.3萬個，高於路透調查預期的710萬個；8月由707.9萬個上修11.1萬個至719萬個。職缺率從4.3%升至4.5%；路透估計，每名失業者對應約1.06個職缺，高於8月的1.02個。

實際聘僱沒有職缺總數顯示得那麼熱絡。聘僱人數由8月的527.1萬增至540.2萬，聘僱率由3.3%升至3.4%。美國勞工統計局（BLS）仍將整體職缺、聘僱與裁員描述為變動不大。這與數據優於市場預期並不衝突：超出經濟學家預測，加上前期上修，足以改變利率預期，但未必代表全體經濟的勞動需求出現統計上顯著的加速。

產業細項並不一致。專業與商業服務職缺增加10.6萬個，不含教育的州與地方政府增加10.4萬個，製造業增加5.4萬個，營建業增加3.6萬個。住宿餐飲聘僱增加15.8萬人，但製造業、專業與商業服務、金融活動及若干政府類別均減少。因此，在部分推升職缺的產業，雇主表達的需求與實際完成的聘僱走向不同。

勞工流動有所改善，解僱則仍低。自願離職由約304.4萬人增至336.5萬人，離職率由1.9%升至2.1%；約32.1萬人的增幅中，住宿餐飲占19.7萬人。裁員與解僱減少約12.7萬人至164.1萬人，為2025年3月以來最低，其中醫療保健與社會援助減少7萬人。總離職人數為531.9萬人，高於前期517.5萬人。8月修正值另將聘僱上修7.9萬人、總離職上修10.5萬人，自願離職下修2.2萬人，裁員則上修12.7萬人。

工廠訂單提供另一項需求訊號。9月月增1.8%，高於預期1.2%；8月增幅也由0.1%上修至0.3%，9月訂單較去年同期增加7.2%。民用飛機與零件訂單大增28.3%，對整體成長貢獻可觀，但排除運輸後，訂單仍月增1.3%，高於預期0.5%，也高於前期修正後的0.4%。

設備需求的強勢涵蓋多個類別。機械訂單月增1.5%，電腦與電子產品月增0.8%、年增14.9%。排除國防與飛機的核心資本財訂單，月增率由0.5%上修至0.6%；出貨則維持月增1.2%。汽車車體、零件與拖車僅增0.1%，電氣設備、家電與零組件則減少0.3%。不含國防的耐久財訂單終值增加2.3%，高於預期2.2%；不含運輸的指標增加0.5%，符合預期。

路透將製造業獲得的支撐歸因於AI基礎設施支出與消費需求，也指出關稅、價格上漲、交貨時間拉長及伊朗衝突仍造成困難。訂單數據強化設備投資持續的理由，卻沒有消除產業間的差異。其他數據也較強：10月物流經理人指數從70.2升至70.7；11月RCM/TIPP經濟樂觀指數由46.8升至48.5，高於預期46.2；截至10月31日當週，Redbook零售銷售年增率由9.3%加速至10.4%。

科技股在投資回報仍不明朗下反彈。半導體指數上漲2.63%，那斯達克100上漲0.68%，標普500上漲0.36%至7,568.92點，儘管多數成分股下跌。VIX回落至20.83。美元指數上升0.12%至101.876，黃金期貨下跌0.74%至每盎司$3,940.20。美國高收益債利差明顯收窄，與股市反彈相呼應。

美債這次回落之前，市場部位已不再那麼偏空。截至10月27日當週，資產管理業者的10年期公債期貨淨多單約達300萬口，依Bloomberg報導為歷史新高。其後，上週未平倉量增加約20萬口，相當於約$160億當期10年期現券。花旗的David Bieber形容，戰術部位已轉向偏擁擠的多頭。這些部位在週二數據公布前便已累積；近期持有久期曝險帶來回報，也有助於解釋為何市場在接近下一批催化事件時，部位較為均衡，而非壓倒性偏空。

## Meta付出更高信用溢酬取得資金

Meta先前討論的跨境融資，已透過$150億美元債發行完成第一步。最高訂單約為發行規模的3.9倍，大致符合今年美國大型科技債發行的平均水準。知情人士指出，早期灰色市場報價利差低於發行定價，顯示投資人雖要求較優厚條件，新債初期反應仍穩健。

五個券別中，最長的2056年到期債券以美債加220個基點定價，較初步討論收窄30個基點，但仍比Meta在4月發行的可比債券寬近90個基點。全案殖利率介於5.85%至7.53%。10年期的6.55%不僅高於AA債平均近1個百分點，也比評級較低的BBB債平均高約0.5個百分點。

這些比較顯示，產業特有的融資疑慮已大幅改變通常的評級與殖利率關係。Bloomberg報導，科技債相對其他投資級債的殖利率溢酬達2003年以來最高，逆轉以往殖利率較低的慣例。Bel Air Investment Advisors的Craig Brothers表示，利差擴大帶來一些紀律，但超大規模雲端業者為取得資金，仍願意支付這些成本。Meta本次交易由花旗與摩根士丹利主辦。

這筆美元債是跨幣別募資計畫的最大部分，總規模預期至少$200億。知情人士表示，首次歐元債發行最快可能於週三接續進行。整體資金需求依然龐大：Bloomberg Intelligence預估，其追蹤的超大規模雲端與新型雲端公司未來三年投資將接近$4.5兆，其中Meta超過$7,400億。這些支出預估的範圍，遠超過此次完成的美元債募資。

近期股價疲弱，使融資來源多元化更為困難。甲骨文目前披露的$99億股票出售以折價11%定價，在週一已完成的債券交易之外，進一步呈現其股權融資成本。Meta規模更大的股權計畫，則結合上週進行的普通股與特別股融資，以及未來在市場出售股票的授權。股價下跌提高了現有股東承擔的融資代價，而債權人同時也要求更高溢酬。

Alphabet正尋求另一種融資架構。初步文件將其列為一筆擬議$15億預付能源市政債的資金收受方，由California Community Choice Financing Authority發債，高盛安排交易。Central Coast Community Energy將取得折價電力，供應加州沿岸從聖塔克魯茲至聖塔芭芭拉的客戶。

預付架構讓資金收受方先取得債券募集款，再隨時間定期付款，以促成公用事業公司的能源交付。若本次參與成行，將是Alphabet繼6月交易後，今年第二次採用此安排；它仍是首家公開參與這類角色的科技公司，過去主要由銀行擔任。今年該類債券已發行約$365億，超過去年$310億的紀錄。這項安排一方面拓展大型科技借款人的融資管道，另一方面也服務於獨立的公用事業採購需求。

資產管理與銀行高層在香港對這輪投資週期提出截然不同的看法。Pimco的Emmanuel Roman估計，AI未來五年的融資需求約$10兆，並警告最終規模可能過度龐大。摩根士丹利的Ted Pick認為，$10兆至$15兆的建設規模是合理可能的，而且產業仍在發展初期。高盛的David Solomon預期融資活動將持續，但也承認過程難免受挫。

Apollo對投資經濟效益的評估提出更具體的警訊。總裁Jim Zelter表示，公司計畫以較防禦的方式進行AI相關投資；運算需求上升與能力改善較為明確，但未來定價與回報的走向尚不清楚。這項區分也呼應當天初級市場的結果：Meta拿到大筆訂單，但融資價格反映的是未來現金創造能力仍有疑問，而非缺乏買家。

## 再融資與重整反映信用需求分化

歐洲槓桿融資市場的條件較不寬鬆。高盛與桑坦德因認購不足，撤回能源基礎設施與服務公司Iqony的€5.5億再融資貸款。這筆BB評級交易原擬取代一組銀行持有的債務，既有債務將繼續保留。

本案屬於把握市場機會的融資，以盡力銷售方式推介，沒有包銷或銀行自有資金承諾。知情人士表示，投資人對其私募股權股東Asterion Industrial Partners較不熟悉，也可能限制需求。因此，撤案中斷的是擬議再融資，並未撤走Iqony現有資金。這是一週內第二筆撤回的歐洲槓桿貸款，前一筆是Partners Group收購Aroma-Zone的融資。

銀行仍在籌組新的收購融資。Cinven同意向凱雷與PAI Partners收購女性健康藥廠Theramex，據報估值約€26億。約€15億融資正在準備中，可能採槓桿貸款與循環額度，高盛、摩根士丹利及Jefferies預計扮演主要角色。對機構投資人的聯貸銷售預計於年底或明年初進行。目前市場對融資案仍有選擇，這項協議則增添了潛在供給。

美國方面，摩根士丹利推出$23億貸款，支應Michael Dell家族辦公室與Sequence Holdings收購Baldwin Insurance Group。融資包括$20億定期貸款及$3億延後動用定期貸款，兩者均為7年期；初步討論的利差為基準利率加350個基點，發行價格為面額的99%。另有$7.5億第二順位擔保債務已完成私募。這筆$77億全現金收購預計於2027年第1季完成，貸款承諾截止日為11月12日。

紙漿生產商Mercer International則朝更根本的資產負債表重整邁進。公司計畫依據一份獲逾87%優先票據持有人及多數股東支持的協議，在德州提出預先協議式美國破產法第11章聲請。方案擬將約$11億優先票據轉為股權，使$13億優先票據債務減少約88%；另透過認股權發行籌措$4億，由臨時票據持有人小組的部分成員全額保證承購。

現有股東將取得重整後公司新普通股的8.5%，以及新可轉換特別股的3.5%；重整生效時，原有股票將註銷。公司於10月1日未支付2028年到期票據利息，其寬限期由30天延長至90天，之後才達成這項框架。一筆加拿大循環融資也將於2027年1月到期。Mercer警告，若無替代資金或再融資，營運現金創造能力可能不足以償付。纖維與能源成本上升、關稅及持續現金流出，已壓縮其選項。

Virgin Media O2宣布以營運調整回應債務壓力。這家Liberty Global與西班牙電信合資的公司，計畫停止投資光纖網路，並在2029年前將每年支出削減£8億，其中2027年節省£4億。未來兩年也將尋求削減約30%的人事成本。在多年擴張寬頻網路後，競爭與約£220億債務迫使公司轉向保留現金。職位削減預計多集中於資訊科技與總部職能，但公司未說明人數。

阿根廷能源公司則呈現債務與股權融資的另一種分化。當地資產價格下跌壓抑估值，Genneia將紐約上市延至至少2027年，但仍以本週發行綠色債券為目標。YPF Luz的IPO則因控股股東YPF同意以$4.3億，收購一家由奇異分拆企業所控制的公司持有的約25%股權而擱置；這筆私下退出交易，消除了原先上市的一項主要理由。兩起延後各有不同的直接原因，但更廣泛的市場回落，也使股權融資的吸引力下降。

## 央行對下一次升息看法分歧

澳洲今年第五次升息，將現金利率提高25個基點至4.85%，為18年高點，但6比3的表決顯示，有相當比例委員支持維持不變。澳洲央行總裁Michele Bullock強調，最近幾次升息尚未開始傳導至經濟。聲明也刪除6月以來明確表示必要時願再升息的文字；Bullock則強調，繼續行動或暫停都仍有可能。

市場最初關注的是這份彈性。Bloomberg報導，交易員將明年現金利率達到5.1%的機率下調至約30%；公告前，市場認為5月前達到該水準的機率接近50%。澳幣下跌。澳洲聯邦銀行的Belinda Allen預期，消費減弱與失業率上升將緩和通膨，利率會維持不變至2027年；澳洲國民銀行的Sally Auld則警告，預測幾乎沒有容納通膨高於預期的空間。

官方通膨展望依然惡化。澳洲央行預期，通膨在2027年大部分時間仍將偏高，直到2027年末才回到2%至3%目標區間的上緣，較先前預測晚約三季。另一項基礎通膨預測，則顯示回到區間內的時間比8月預測晚約六個月。官員列出的因素包括燃料與大宗商品成本、國內產能壓力加重、AI投資帶來的科技產品通膨，以及企業轉嫁更高投入成本。

需求端的反向壓力也愈來愈明顯。央行認為金融條件具限制性，預測成長放緩、失業率升幅擴大，住宅市場與消費也將進一步走弱。資料中心活動支撐近期企業投資，但生產力疲弱，已降低估計中不致引發通膨的經濟成長能力。分歧表決反映的是這些相互拉扯的發展，而非對通膨已受控制的信心。

南韓10月CPI整體漲幅略降，但基礎壓力持續。年增率由2.9%降至2.8%，符合Bloomberg調查中位數，仍高於2%目標。核心通膨維持2.8%，高於預測中位數2.7%。Bloomberg Economics的Hyosung Kwon認為，整體通膨放緩部分與中秋節時間變動有關：今年落在9月，去年則在10月。

南韓生產與家庭需求的分化仍明顯。第3季產出季增1%，高於預期0.8%；設備投資增加4.1%，民間消費卻減少0.2%。10月經工作日調整的出口年增約76%，半導體出貨大增259%至$564億。道富的Jiuk Choi預期，南韓央行將把2027年整體與核心通膨預測各上修10至20個基點，並在11月會議升息。目前基準利率為3%，新預測將於11月26日公布。

紐西蘭第3季勞動數據於美國午後較晚公布，更明確指向需求轉弱。失業率達5.7%，為2015年以來最高，高於經濟學家與紐西蘭央行均預估的5.5%。就業未如預期增加0.4%，反而減少0.1%；勞參率為70.4%，低於預期70.7%。不含加班的民間部門勞動成本季增0.4%，年增率由2.1%降至2%。Kiwibank經濟學家表示，情勢惡化愈來愈支持央行近期暫停於2.75%的決定，儘管央行仍暗示可能進一步緊縮。

歐洲方面，德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel強化了12月升息的理由。他表示，通膨展望較9月預測進一步惡化，而當時預測就已納入再升息一次；除非展望顯著改善，否則幾乎別無選擇。他也保留10月暫停升息的理由：目前第二輪效應仍不多，但反覆的能源衝擊可能愈來愈容易推升薪資要求。

荷蘭央行總裁Olaf Sleijpen表示，僅見些微間接效應；即使短期通膨預期上升，長期預期仍有利。保加利亞的Dimitar Radev另強調，暫停並不代表緊縮週期結束。Bloomberg市場報導顯示，德國10年期殖利率上升4個基點至3.33%，英國則上升7個基點至5.26%。

Bloomberg Economics一項新分析，對較後期的通膨路徑得出不同結論。Andrej Sokol以AI分析歐洲央行官員演說與訪談的新聞標題，結合非線性預測工具，結果顯示通膨第4季接近4%，之後於2027年中降至2.4%、年底降至1.7%。這是由官員談話推導的模型解讀，並非新的官方預測；其結果低於歐洲央行最新預估的2027年平均2.5%。這凸顯近期再升息的理由，與日後通膨可能低於目標之間的落差。

加拿大央行總裁Tiff Macklem不認同現行聯邦財政計畫已妨礙抑制通膨。他指出經濟仍有閒置產能，支出重點也在投資而非經常性開支；無論是財政不可持續性外溢至市場，或財政與貨幣政策衝突，目前都未達到令他憂慮的標準。BMO的Doug Porter持不同意見，認為聯邦與省政府廣泛的支持措施，正與上週升息相牴觸。他表示，若貿易協議能降低關稅與不確定性，可能改變看法。川普另表示，與加拿大的協議已接近達成；總理Mark Carney則說，團隊未來幾週仍將持續談判。

## 財政可信度與國家關聯信用面臨新考驗

巴西最新經濟學家調查顯示，選舉衝擊持續改變的不只是下一次會議，而是更長期的政策預期。央行每週調查將12月Selic利率預測由13.25%提高至13.5%，2027年底由11.75%提高至12.5%，2028年由10%提高至11%，2029年則升至10.25%。截至2029年的通膨預估，也進一步高於3%目標。公布後，雷亞爾一度下跌1.4%，較長天期利率期貨在早盤上升。

財政部長Dario Durigan反駁悲觀預期，表示政府有意改善公共帳目，尋求平衡財政的方法。不過，調查變化仍意味著本已承壓的借款人，未來融資負擔可能更重。巴西7月農村信用餘額為8,850億雷亞爾，其中央行列為有問題的貸款高達創紀錄的2,080億雷亞爾，涵蓋逾期、拖欠及重新協商貸款。

政府暫行措施撥出260億雷亞爾支持補貼貸款，但農業代表希望取得更廣泛的紓困。若未獲國會批准，措施將於11月失效；一個區域農業遊說團體表示，方案將主要貸款機構排除在重新協商之外。IMEA預期，馬托格羅索州本季與下一季的種植面積擴張有限。Mapa Capital的Manoel Pereira de Queiroz指出，即使基準利率下降，銀行風險溢酬上升仍使信用昂貴。依Serasa Experian資料，第2季破產保護聲請季減5.5%，可能部分受重新協商幫助；但儘管有此改善，債務存量與融資成本仍構成困難。

中國最新的華發相關市場數字，反映的是更廣泛的外溢影響，而非又一次新的支付違約。截至週一的兩個交易日，境內3年期AAA公司債基準殖利率上升10.3個基點，為2024年10月以來最大兩日升幅，週二上午則大致持平。華發地產子公司履行週一到期付款後，華發2027年到期離岸人民幣債回升至面額約63%。公開債務償付改善之後，投資人仍在評估，資產變現與持續付款能否控制流動性壓力，抑或展期會引發對國有借款人更廣泛的重新評估。

中國當局也針對另一項市場失衡採取行動。中國人民銀行宣布，自11月15日起，銀行外匯存款準備金率由4%提高至6%，以吸收外幣流動性。在岸人民幣一度貶值0.4%至每美元6.6728元，結束連續13天升值。澳盛銀行的Zhaopeng Xing估計，此舉將回收約$240億，相較今年每月約$300億的淨售匯規模仍屬溫和。重啟股市支持工具也未立即帶來反彈：滬深300下跌0.2%，科創50下跌3.8%。

比利時再獲警告，即使政府得以延續，所需財政調整仍相當龐大。經濟合作暨發展組織（OECD）指出，政府規劃2029年前節省相當於GDP的1.5%仍不足夠，須在2035年前再削減相當於GDP的3.5%，才能將債務穩定在GDP約110%。初步預測顯示，2027年赤字為GDP的5.1%，僅略低於2025年的5.2%。總理Bart De Wever週一已提出辭呈，國王則暫緩決定，先與聯合政府各黨磋商。面對利息、人口老化、國防與氣候轉型成本增加，OECD主張及早落實支出節制，並擴大稅基。

智利退休基金數據則呈現10月殖利率下降的新影響。保守型E基金在9月虧損4.9%後，10月上漲3.2%，使2026年虧損縮小至7.6%；C與D基金分別上漲1%與1.8%。退休金監理機關先前估計，截至10月20日，收取固定利率交換部位的市值評價損失約$70億，低於9月底的$101億。經理人辯稱，這些部位是為保障長期退休收入，但損失已引發監管檢視。單月回升減輕了損害，仍未消除保守型儲蓄者今年的負報酬。

## 後續市場焦點

選舉開票在本次固定收益交易時段結束後展開，首批投票所於美東時間下午6時關閉。國會控制權將左右支出與債務上限談判，但分立政府未必代表借款下降。花旗與高盛經濟學家認為，共和黨優勢微弱，加上財政保守派反對，權力交接前達成債務上限協議的可能性有限。債務上限可能在2027年前幾個月觸及，經濟學家估計最終融資期限落在下半年。高盛認為，兩黨協議可能同時增加國防與非國防支出。較近的財政期限，則是臨時政府撥款於12月11日到期。

美國財政部將於11月4日美東時間上午8時30分公布再融資安排，焦點在於官員是否改變舉債期限組合。摩根資產管理的Bob Michele主張取消20年期公債，將更多融資轉向國庫券，理由是貨幣市場資產規模深厚。Bloomberg調查中沒有任何交易商將直接取消20年期公債列為基本情境。在長端一週表現落後短天期之後，投資人的提議與財政部最終指引之間的差別尤其重要。

週三美國數據將在9月職缺與訂單轉強之後，補上10月證據。美東時間上午8時15分的ADP就業預期增加6.9萬人，前值9萬人。上午9時45分公布標普全球服務業PMI終值，預期57.9，前值58.8；上午10時的ISM服務業PMI預期54.8，前值54.9。9月貿易逆差預期為$1,080億，前值$1,056億。服務業活動與就業將特別有助於判斷，近期製造業與職缺的強勢是否擴及更廣範圍。

週四初領失業救濟金人數預期19.6萬人，前值19.4萬人。第3季生產力預期增加2.5%，單位勞動成本增加0.7%，將提供產出效率與就業成本的另一組比較。週五10月非農就業預期增加6.5萬人，前值2.9萬人；U-3整體失業率預期維持4.2%，平均時薪預期月增0.3%、年增2.9%。這些指標將讓市場區分實際就業創造與薪資壓力，以及帶動週二行情的職缺與自願離職訊號。

市場預期英國央行週四升息至4%，但對之後的路徑分歧更大。貨幣市場反映明年夏末前利率至少達4.75%，經濟學家共識則認為，2027年第1季再升息的機率僅五成。央行預測及其對能源成本傳導的處理，將決定哪條路徑獲得較多支持。週三歐元區通膨預期整體為4%、核心為2.5%。加拿大週四預算案則緊接在Macklem為投資導向財政支持辯護之後，其中包括擬以五年C$360億擴大企業支出可立即認列沖銷的範圍。

巴西週三決策將顯示，官員是否如目前多數分析師預期，在13.75%暫停降息。Meta可能首發歐元債，以及Baldwin貸款11月12日的承諾截止日，將分別檢驗初級信用市場需求。歐洲央行總裁提名截止日為11月6日，為領導層交接增添一個明確的程序時點。另據週二報導，卡達調停者預期，最新美國與伊朗提案的回覆將於兩天內到來。伊朗否認談判已取得報導所稱進展，美國又在夜間空襲格什姆島，使外交斡旋仍活躍但不確定；能源成本是否持續偏高，對即將開會的央行依然重要。

overall_summary.headline: 美國需求轉強、實質殖利率上升，美債漲勢逆轉
overall_summary.session_narrative:
9月職缺達752.3萬個，高於預期710萬個；工廠訂單增加1.8%，也超過預期1.2%，使美債回吐油價下跌帶動的早盤漲幅。8月數據上修進一步強化這兩項意外強勢，但聘僱與產業細項仍不一致。10年期殖利率上升4.96個基點至4.9621%，其中實質殖利率貢獻4.47個基點，通膨補償僅貢獻0.49個基點。中天期債券領跌，但10年期殖利率仍低於一週前與一個月前。

Meta完成當天美國唯一一筆投資級債發行，募得$150億，吸引最高$580億訂單。10年期債券殖利率為6.55%，高於同評級AA債近1個百分點。認購踴躍顯示公司仍能取得資金，但未消除市場對AI支出現金回報的疑慮。半導體股反彈、美國高收益債利差明顯收窄，也顯示當天市場風險偏好有所回升。

澳洲在分歧表決下升息，同時保留暫停空間；歐洲官員則仍考慮再度升息。接下來，美國服務業與非農就業數據將檢驗需求韌性是否擴及職缺與製造業之外，財政部即將公布的指引則將釐清舉債期限組合。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries fell as stronger-than-expected U.S. job openings and factory orders interrupted the bond market's recent recovery, overcoming an early rally driven by falling oil prices. The 10-year yield rose 4.96 basis points to 4.9621%, with higher real yields accounting for most of the increase. A rebound in semiconductor shares also reduced the session's defensive character, although investors continued to demand substantial compensation to finance the artificial-intelligence investment boom.

Meta raised $15 billion in the day's only U.S. investment-grade bond offering, attracting as much as $58 billion of orders. Its 10-year debt yielded 6.55%, almost a percentage point above similarly rated AA bonds. Strong demand and expensive funding were both features of the transaction: investors were willing to supply capital, but on terms reflecting their growing concern about the industry's spending requirements.

The economic releases gave the rates selloff a firmer foundation than an equity rebound alone. September vacancies exceeded consensus and August was revised higher; factory orders also beat expectations, with strength extending beyond aircraft. Neither release established uniform acceleration across employers or industries. Their detail nevertheless made an imminent deterioration in U.S. demand harder to assume, even as Australia's divided rate increase and fresh European policy comments showed central banks weighing persistent inflation against increasingly visible restraints on activity.

## Labor Demand Reverses the Treasury Rally

Oil initially supplied another reason to buy government bonds. WTI briefly fell below $94 a barrel, a three-week low, and the 10-year Treasury yield declined about 2 basis points. The direction changed after the September Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey: Bloomberg's intraday account put the 10-year yield at a session high of 4.97% within minutes of the release, more than 5 basis points higher on the day. ING's Padhraic Garvey described the figures as firm and the upward yield response as appropriate.

The closing adjustment was broad but concentrated in intermediate maturities. The five-year yield rose 5.32 basis points to 4.7623%, the two-year increased 3.72 basis points to 4.6309%, and the 30-year added 4.08 basis points to 5.3265%. The two- to 10-year gap widened 1.24 basis points to 33.12 basis points. That was a modest steepening through a selloff, rather than a disproportionate repricing of the shortest coupon maturity.

The 10-year TIPS real yield increased 4.47 basis points to 2.6542%, while 10-year inflation compensation rose only 0.49 basis point to 2.3079%. Most of the nominal-yield increase therefore came from real yields, consistent with a session in which evidence of resilient demand mattered more than a renewed surge in longer-term inflation compensation. Brent finished down 0.33% at $104.42, while WTI recovered to $96.76, up 0.31%.

The daily reversal left much of the preceding recovery intact. The 10-year yield remained 3.46 basis points below its week-earlier level and 31.09 basis points below its month-earlier level. Two-year yields were down 10.6 basis points over the week, whereas the 30-year was 1.62 basis points higher. The longer end had participated less fully in the weekly rally, leaving the curve sensitive to both the economic outlook and the allocation of government borrowing across maturities.

JOLTS supplied a numerical upside surprise alongside a more restrained official assessment of the overall labor market. Vacancies reached 7.523 million in September, above the 7.100 million Reuters consensus. August openings were revised up by 111,000 to 7.190 million from 7.079 million. The vacancy rate rose to 4.5% from 4.3%, and Reuters put openings per unemployed worker at approximately 1.06, compared with 1.02 in August.

Actual hiring remained less buoyant than the headline vacancies might suggest. Hires totaled 5.402 million, against 5.271 million in August, with the hiring rate moving to 3.4% from 3.3%. The Bureau of Labor Statistics described overall openings, hiring and layoffs as little changed. Its characterization matters alongside the market surprise: a result above economists' forecasts and an upward revision can alter rate expectations without establishing a statistically significant, economy-wide acceleration in labor demand.

The industry detail was uneven. Openings increased by 106,000 in professional and business services, 104,000 in state and local government excluding education, 54,000 in manufacturing and 36,000 in construction. Hiring rose 158,000 in accommodation and food services but declined in manufacturing, professional and business services, financial activities and several government categories. Employers' stated demand and their completed hiring were consequently moving differently in some of the sectors contributing to the vacancy gain.

Worker mobility improved while dismissals remained subdued. Quits rose to 3.365 million from approximately 3.044 million, taking the quits rate to 2.1% from 1.9%. Accommodation and food services accounted for 197,000 of the approximately 321,000 increase. Layoffs and discharges fell by approximately 127,000 to 1.641 million, their lowest level since March 2025; healthcare and social assistance contributed a 70,000 decline. Total separations were 5.319 million, compared with 5.175 million. August revisions also raised hires by 79,000 and separations by 105,000, while reducing quits by 22,000 and increasing layoffs by 127,000.

Factory orders added a separate demand signal. September orders increased 1.8% on the month, exceeding the 1.2% consensus, and August's gain was revised to 0.3% from 0.1%. Orders were 7.2% higher than a year earlier. Civilian aircraft and parts bookings jumped 28.3%, making an important contribution to the headline, but orders excluding transportation rose 1.3%, against expectations of 0.5% and a revised 0.4% increase previously.

Equipment demand extended across several categories. Machinery orders rose 1.5%, while computers and electronic products increased 0.8% on the month and 14.9% on the year. Core capital goods orders, excluding defense and aircraft, were revised to a 0.6% monthly gain from 0.5%; shipments rose an unrevised 1.2%. Motor vehicle bodies, parts and trailers increased just 0.1%, and electrical equipment, appliances and components fell 0.3%. Final durable-goods orders excluding defense rose 2.3%, above the 2.2% consensus, while the excluding-transportation measure increased 0.5%, as expected.

Reuters attributed support for manufacturing to AI infrastructure spending and consumer demand, while noting continued difficulties from tariffs, higher prices, longer delivery times and the Iran conflict. The orders figures strengthened the case for continuing equipment investment without erasing those sector differences. Other releases were also firmer: the October Logistics Managers Index rose to 70.7 from 70.2, November's RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism Index increased to 48.5 from 46.8 against a 46.2 consensus, and Redbook sales growth accelerated to 10.4% year on year from 9.3% for the week ended October 31.

Technology shares recovered despite continuing uncertainty over the returns on investment. The semiconductor index gained 2.63%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.68% and the S&P 500 advanced 0.36% to 7,568.92, even as most constituents declined. The VIX eased to 20.83. The Dollar Index rose 0.12% to 101.876 and gold futures fell 0.74% to $3,940.20 an ounce. U.S. high-yield spreads tightened noticeably, providing a credit-market counterpart to the equity rebound.

The retreat in Treasuries came after positioning had become less bearish. In the week through October 27, asset managers' net long position in 10-year futures reached about 3 million contracts, a record in Bloomberg's account. Open interest subsequently rose around 200,000 contracts last week, equivalent to roughly $16 billion of the current 10-year cash note. Citigroup's David Bieber described tactical positioning as having moved into extended longs. That accumulation preceded Tuesday's data and helps explain why a market that had recently rewarded duration was approaching the next catalysts with more balanced, rather than overwhelmingly short, exposure.

## Meta Secures Capital at Higher Credit Premiums

Meta's dollar sale converted its previously discussed cross-border financing into a completed $15 billion transaction. Peak orders reached about 3.9 times the issue size, roughly in line with the average for major U.S. technology bond offerings this year. Early gray-market quotations were tighter than the pricing spreads, according to people familiar with the transaction, giving the new bonds a firmer initial reception after investors had required generous terms.

The longest of the five tranches, due in 2056, priced at 220 basis points over Treasuries, 30 basis points inside initial discussions. That remained almost 90 basis points wider than a comparable Meta issue in April. Across the offering, yields ranged from 5.85% to 7.53%. The 10-year's 6.55% yield was not only almost a percentage point above the AA average but roughly half a percentage point above the average for lower-rated BBB debt.

Those comparisons show how substantially sector-specific financing concerns have altered the usual ratings hierarchy. Bloomberg reported technology bonds trading at their largest yield premium to other investment-grade debt since 2003, reversing their customary discount. Bel Air Investment Advisors' Craig Brothers said wider spreads were imposing some discipline, but hyperscalers remained willing to pay them to access capital. Citi and Morgan Stanley ran Meta's transaction.

The offering forms the largest portion of fundraising expected to reach at least $20 billion across currencies. A debut euro transaction could follow as soon as Wednesday, according to people familiar with the plans. The financing requirement remains substantial: Bloomberg Intelligence expects its group of hyperscalers and neocloud companies to invest almost $4.5 trillion over the next three years, including more than $740 billion at Meta. Those are spending expectations, extending well beyond the capital raised in the completed dollar sale.

The equity market's recent weakness complicates the effort to diversify that funding. Oracle's now-reported $9.9 billion share sale was priced at an 11% discount, a new measure of the cost of its equity funding alongside Monday's already completed bond transaction. Meta's much larger equity program combines common and preferred financing undertaken last week with permission for future market sales. Lower share prices make that additional channel more expensive for existing shareholders just as creditors seek higher premiums.

Alphabet is pursuing another financing structure, with preliminary documents identifying it as funding recipient for a planned $1.5 billion prepaid-energy municipal bond offering. The California Community Choice Financing Authority will issue the bonds, Goldman Sachs is arranging the transaction, and Central Coast Community Energy will receive discounted electricity to sell to customers along California's coast from Santa Cruz to Santa Barbara.

Under the prepaid structure, the funding recipient receives bond proceeds upfront and makes periodic payments over time to facilitate energy delivery to the utility. Alphabet's proposed participation would be its second this year following a June transaction, and it remains the first technology company publicly participating in a role historically occupied mainly by banks. The sector has issued about $36.5 billion this year, already exceeding last year's $31 billion record. The arrangement expands the range of funding channels available to a large technology borrower while serving a distinct utility procurement purpose.

Asset managers and bank executives offered sharply different assessments of the investment cycle in Hong Kong. Pimco's Emmanuel Roman estimated AI financing needs at about $10 trillion over five years and warned that the eventual amount could become excessive. Morgan Stanley's Ted Pick described a $10 trillion-$15 trillion buildout as plausible and the industry as still early in its development. Goldman Sachs' David Solomon expected continued financing activity while acknowledging setbacks along the way.

Apollo added a more specific caution about underwriting the economics. President Jim Zelter said the manager planned a more defensive approach to AI-related investments: rising computing needs and improving capabilities were clearer than the future path of pricing and returns. That distinction fits the day's primary-market result. Meta found a large order book, but the price of that access reflected unresolved questions about future cash generation rather than an absence of buyers.

## Refinancings and Restructurings Test Uneven Credit Appetite

Europe's leveraged-finance market provided a less accommodating result. Goldman Sachs and Santander withdrew a €550 million refinancing loan for energy infrastructure and services company Iqony after failing to attract enough interest. The BB-rated transaction had been intended to replace debt held by a club of banks; that existing debt will remain in place.

The financing was opportunistic and marketed on a best-efforts basis, without underwriting or bank balance-sheet commitments. People familiar with the process said demand may also have been constrained by investors' lesser familiarity with sponsor Asterion Industrial Partners. The withdrawal thus interrupted a proposed refinancing rather than removing Iqony's existing funding. It was the second European leveraged-loan deal pulled in a week, following financing for Partners Group's purchase of Aroma-Zone.

Banks continued assembling new acquisition packages. Cinven agreed to buy women's-health pharmaceutical company Theramex from Carlyle and PAI Partners at a reported valuation of about €2.6 billion. Around €1.5 billion of financing is being prepared, likely through leveraged loans and a revolving facility, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies expected to take leading roles. Institutional syndication is expected toward year-end or early next year. The agreement adds prospective supply even while current distribution conditions remain selective.

In the U.S., Morgan Stanley launched $2.3 billion of loans for Michael Dell's family office and Sequence Holdings' acquisition of Baldwin Insurance Group. The package comprises a $2 billion term loan and a $300 million delayed-draw term loan, both maturing in seven years. Initial discussions put the margin at 350 basis points over the benchmark and the issue price at 99 cents on the dollar. A further $750 million of second-lien secured debt has already been privately placed. The $7.7 billion all-cash acquisition is expected to close in Q1 2027, with loan commitments due November 12.

Mercer International moved toward a more fundamental balance-sheet restructuring. The pulp producer plans a prepackaged Chapter 11 filing in Texas under an agreement supported by holders of more than 87% of its senior notes and a majority of shareholders. The proposal would exchange approximately $1.1 billion of senior notes for equity, reducing the $1.3 billion senior-note debt by about 88%, and provide $400 million through a rights offering fully backstopped by certain members of an ad hoc noteholder group.

Existing shareholders would receive 8.5% of the reorganized company's new common stock and 3.5% of its new convertible preferred stock; their existing shares would be canceled when the restructuring becomes effective. The agreed framework follows an October 1 missed interest payment on notes due in 2028, for which the grace period was extended to 90 days from 30. A Canadian revolving facility also matures in January 2027, and Mercer warned that cash generation was unlikely to cover it without alternative funding or refinancing. Rising fiber and energy costs, tariffs and persistent cash burn had narrowed its options.

Virgin Media O2 announced an operating response to debt pressure. The Liberty Global and Telefonica joint venture plans to stop investing in its fiber network and reduce annual expenditures by £800 million by 2029, including £400 million of savings in 2027. It will seek to cut labor costs by approximately 30% over the next two years. Competition and roughly £22 billion of debt are pushing the operator toward cash conservation after years of broadband expansion; most job reductions are expected in IT and head-office functions, although the company did not specify a headcount.

Argentina's energy companies displayed a different division between debt and equity access. Genneia has deferred a New York listing until at least 2027 as falling local asset prices weigh on valuation, but is targeting a green bond sale this week. YPF Luz's IPO was shelved after controlling shareholder YPF agreed to buy the roughly 25% stake held by a company controlled by a General Electric spin-off for $430 million. That private exit removed a principal reason for the planned listing. The two postponements therefore reflect different immediate causes, even as a broader market retreat makes equity financing less attractive.

## Central Banks Diverge on the Next Increase

Australia delivered its fifth rate increase of the year, lifting the cash rate 25 basis points to 4.85%, its highest in 18 years, but the six-to-three vote revealed a substantial minority favoring a hold. Governor Michele Bullock emphasized that the most recent increases had not yet begun flowing through the economy. The statement also dropped language, used since June, explicitly declaring a willingness to raise rates further if needed, while Bullock stressed that both further action and a pause remained possible.

The immediate market response focused on that flexibility. Bloomberg reported traders reducing the probability of a 5.1% cash rate next year to about 30%, from an almost 50% chance of reaching that level by May before the announcement. The Australian dollar fell. Commonwealth Bank's Belinda Allen expects rates to remain unchanged into 2027 as weaker consumption and higher unemployment moderate inflation, while National Australia Bank's Sally Auld warned that the forecast left little room for an upside inflation surprise.

The official inflation outlook nonetheless deteriorated. The RBA expects inflation to remain elevated through much of 2027 and return to the upper edge of its 2%-3% target only in late 2027, approximately three quarters later than previously forecast. Its separate underlying-inflation forecast put the return inside the band about six months later than in August. Officials cited fuel and commodity costs, greater domestic capacity pressure, technology-goods inflation associated with AI investment, and firms passing through higher input costs.

The opposing pressure is increasingly visible in demand. The RBA judges financial conditions restrictive, forecasts slower growth and a larger increase in unemployment, and expects housing and consumption to weaken further. Data-center activity supports near-term business investment, but weak productivity has reduced the economy's estimated noninflationary growth capacity. The split vote reflects those competing developments rather than confidence that inflation has already been contained.

South Korea's October CPI also showed persistent underlying pressure despite a slightly lower headline. Annual inflation eased to 2.8% from 2.9%, matching Bloomberg's survey median and remaining above the 2% target. Core inflation held at 2.8%, exceeding the 2.7% median forecast. Bloomberg Economics' Hyosung Kwon attributed part of the headline slowdown to the changing timing of Chuseok, which fell in September this year and October last year.

The production and household-demand split remained pronounced. Q3 output rose 1% quarterly against expectations of 0.8%, with facility investment up 4.1% but private consumption down 0.2%. Working-day-adjusted exports increased about 76% annually in October, and semiconductor shipments rose 259% to $56.4 billion. State Street's Jiuk Choi expects the Bank of Korea to raise its 2027 headline and core inflation forecasts by 10-20 basis points and increase rates at its November meeting. The bank currently holds its benchmark at 3%, with new forecasts due November 26.

New Zealand's Q3 labor figures, published late in the U.S. afternoon, pointed more clearly toward weakening demand. Unemployment reached 5.7%, its highest since 2015, against both economists' and the RBNZ's 5.5% expectation. Employment contracted 0.1% rather than rising the expected 0.4%, and participation was 70.4%, below the 70.7% forecast. Private-sector labor costs excluding overtime rose 0.4% quarterly, with annual growth slowing to 2% from 2.1%. Kiwibank economists said the deterioration increasingly justified the central bank's recent pause at 2.75%, despite its signal that further tightening remained likely.

In Europe, Joachim Nagel sharpened the December case. The Bundesbank president said the inflation outlook had worsened since September's projections, which already incorporated another increase. Unless that outlook improved significantly, he saw little alternative to raising rates. He also preserved the reason for October's pause: few second-round effects had appeared so far, although repeated energy shocks could increasingly feed into wage demands.

Dutch Governor Olaf Sleijpen described only a hint of indirect effects and said long-term inflation expectations remained favorable, even as short-term expectations rose. Bulgaria's Dimitar Radev separately emphasized that the pause did not end the tightening cycle. Germany's 10-year yield rose 4 basis points to 3.33% in Bloomberg's market account; Britain's increased 7 basis points to 5.26%.

A new Bloomberg Economics exercise reached a different conclusion about the later inflation path. Andrej Sokol used AI analysis of headlines from ECB speeches and interviews together with a nonlinear forecasting tool. The results implied inflation approaching 4% in Q4, then easing to 2.4% by mid-2027 and 1.7% by year-end. That is a model-derived interpretation of officials' communications, below the ECB's latest projected 2027 average of 2.5%, rather than a new official forecast. It highlights the distance between the near-term case for another increase and the prospect of eventual undershooting.

Canada's Tiff Macklem rejected the view that existing federal fiscal plans were already obstructing inflation control. He pointed to spare capacity and an emphasis on investment rather than operating spending, and said neither fiscal unsustainability spilling into markets nor fiscal-monetary conflict currently met his criteria for concern. BMO's Doug Porter disagreed, arguing that broad federal and provincial support was working against last week's rate increase. Porter said a trade agreement reducing tariffs and uncertainty could change his view. Trump separately said an agreement with Canada was close, while Prime Minister Mark Carney said teams would continue negotiating over the coming weeks.

## Fiscal Credibility and State-Linked Credit Face New Tests

Brazil's latest economist survey showed the election shock continuing to alter expected policy well beyond the next meeting. The central bank's weekly survey raised the December Selic forecast to 13.5% from 13.25%, the end-2027 estimate to 12.5% from 11.75%, and the 2028 projection to 11% from 10%. The 2029 forecast increased to 10.25%. Inflation estimates also moved further above the 3% target through 2029. The real fell as much as 1.4% after publication and longer-dated rate futures rose in morning trading.

Finance Minister Dario Durigan pushed back, saying the government intended to improve the public accounts and find ways to balance its fiscal position. The survey shift nonetheless raises the prospective financing burden for borrowers already under pressure. Brazil had 885 billion reais of rural credit outstanding in July, including an unprecedented 208 billion reais classified by the central bank as problematic, encompassing overdue, delinquent or renegotiated loans.

Growers' representatives are seeking broader relief than a provisional measure allocating 26 billion reais to support subsidized lending. That measure expires in November without congressional approval, and a regional farm lobby said it excluded major lenders from renegotiation. IMEA expects limited crop-area expansion this season and next in Mato Grosso, while Mapa Capital's Manoel Pereira de Queiroz said rising bank risk premiums were keeping credit expensive even when benchmark rates declined. Bankruptcy-protection filings did fall 5.5% quarterly in Q2, according to Serasa Experian, potentially helped by renegotiations; the credit stock and financing cost remained difficult despite that improvement.

China's newest Huafa-related market figures measured broader spillover rather than another fresh payment failure. Over the two sessions through Monday, benchmark three-year local AAA corporate yields rose 10.3 basis points, their largest two-day increase since October 2024, before remaining little changed Tuesday morning. Huafa's offshore yuan bonds due in 2027 recovered to about 63% of face value after its property arm met payments due Monday. That improvement in public-debt servicing left investors assessing whether asset monetization and continued payments could contain the liquidity strain or whether extensions would prompt wider reassessment of state-owned borrowers.

Chinese authorities also acted on a different market imbalance. The PBOC announced an increase in banks' foreign-exchange reserve requirement to 6% from 4%, effective November 15, to absorb foreign-currency liquidity. The onshore yuan weakened as much as 0.4% to 6.6728 per dollar, ending a 13-day winning streak. ANZ's Zhaopeng Xing estimated the measure would withdraw about $24 billion, modest relative to monthly net foreign-exchange sales of approximately $30 billion this year. Revived equity-support facilities did not produce an immediate stock recovery: the CSI 300 fell 0.2% and the Star 50 dropped 3.8%.

Belgium received a new warning about the scale of fiscal adjustment needed even if its government survives. The OECD said planned savings of 1.5% of GDP by 2029 were insufficient and additional cuts equal to 3.5% of GDP by 2035 were necessary to stabilize debt around 110% of GDP. Its preliminary forecast put the deficit at 5.1% in 2027, barely below 2025's 5.2%. Prime Minister Bart De Wever had offered his resignation Monday; the king deferred a decision while consulting coalition parties. The OECD favors front-loaded spending restraint alongside a broader tax base, citing rising interest, ageing, defense and climate-transition costs.

Chilean pension figures supplied a fresh measure of the effect of October's lower yields. The conservative E fund gained 3.2% during the month after losing 4.9% in September, narrowing its 2026 loss to 7.6%; C and D funds rose 1% and 1.8%. The pension regulator had put receiver-swap mark-to-market losses at about $7 billion on October 20, down from $10.1 billion at September's end. Managers defend the positions as protection for long-term retirement income, while the losses have prompted regulatory scrutiny. The monthly recovery reduced the damage without eliminating the year's negative return for conservative savers.

## Forward Market Significance

Election counting begins after the completed fixed-income session, with the first polls closing at 6 p.m. Eastern. Congressional control will shape negotiations over spending and the debt limit, but a divided government need not mean lower borrowing. Citi and Goldman Sachs economists see limited prospects for a pre-handover debt-limit agreement, given thin Republican margins and opposition among fiscal conservatives. The limit could be reached in the first months of 2027, with economists placing the eventual financing deadline in the second half. Goldman argues that a bipartisan bargain could raise both defense and nondefense spending. December 11's expiry of temporary government funding is the nearer fiscal deadline.

Treasury's November 4 refunding announcement, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Eastern, will test whether officials change the maturity mix. JPMorgan Asset Management's Bob Michele urged eliminating the 20-year bond and directing more financing toward bills, citing the depth of money-market assets. No dealer in Bloomberg's survey treats outright abolition as its base case. The distinction between an investor proposal and Treasury's eventual guidance matters after a week in which the long end has lagged shorter maturities.

Wednesday's U.S. releases will add October evidence to September's stronger vacancies and orders. ADP employment at 8:15 a.m. Eastern is expected to rise 69,000 after 90,000. Final S&P Global Services PMI follows at 9:45 a.m., with consensus at 57.9 after 58.8, before the headline ISM Services PMI at 10 a.m., expected at 54.8 after 54.9. The trade balance is expected to show a $108 billion September deficit, compared with $105.6 billion. Services activity and employment will be especially relevant to whether the latest manufacturing and vacancy strength extends more broadly.

Thursday's initial jobless claims consensus is 196,000 after 194,000. Q3 productivity is expected to rise 2.5%, with unit labor costs up 0.7%, providing a separate comparison between output efficiency and employment costs. Friday's October payroll consensus is 65,000 after 29,000, with the headline U-3 unemployment rate expected to remain 4.2%. Average hourly earnings are expected to rise 0.3% monthly and 2.9% annually. Those measures will distinguish actual job creation and wage pressure from the openings and quits that moved Tuesday's market.

The Bank of England's Thursday decision carries a larger disagreement about what follows an expected increase to 4%. Money markets price at least 4.75% by the end of next summer, whereas the economist consensus sees only an even chance of another increase in Q1 2027. The bank's forecasts and treatment of energy pass-through will determine how much support it gives either path. Euro-area inflation is expected Wednesday at 4% headline and 2.5% core. Canada's Thursday budget follows Macklem's defense of investment-led fiscal support, including a proposed C$36 billion, five-year expansion of immediate business write-offs.

Brazil's Wednesday decision will show whether policymakers pause easing at 13.75%, as most analysts now expect. Meta's prospective euro debut and the Baldwin loan's November 12 commitment deadline offer distinct tests of primary credit demand. ECB presidential nominations are due November 6, adding a dated procedural step to the leadership transition. Separately, Qatar's mediators expect responses to the latest U.S.-Iran proposals within two days of Tuesday's account. Iran's denial of reported progress and overnight U.S. strikes on Qeshm leave diplomacy active but uncertain, with the persistence of energy costs still consequential for the central banks approaching their next decisions.

section_summaries.summary: Stronger vacancies and factory orders made an imminent deterioration in U.S. demand harder to assume, outweighing the early support from falling oil. Higher real yields drove most of the Treasury adjustment. Meta's successful but expensive financing and a semiconductor rebound showed renewed willingness to take risk without removing concern over AI spending requirements.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries surrendered an early oil-led rally after September job openings reached 7.523 million against a 7.100 million consensus and factory orders rose 1.8%, exceeding the 1.2% forecast. August revisions reinforced both surprises, although hiring and industry detail remained uneven. The 10-year yield rose 4.96 basis points to 4.9621%; real yields contributed 4.47 basis points and inflation compensation just 0.49 basis point. Intermediate maturities led the selloff, while the 10-year yield remained below its week- and month-earlier levels.

Meta raised $15 billion in the day's only U.S. investment-grade offering, drawing as much as $58 billion of orders. Its 10-year debt yielded 6.55%, almost a percentage point above similarly rated AA bonds. The strong reception preserved access to capital without resolving concerns about the cash returns on AI spending. Semiconductor shares rebounded and U.S. high-yield spreads tightened noticeably, giving the session a less defensive character.

Australia raised rates on a divided vote while leaving room for a pause, and European officials kept another increase in view. U.S. services and payroll figures now test whether the demand resilience extends beyond vacancies and manufacturing, alongside Treasury's forthcoming guidance on the maturity mix of borrowing.
